newsitem.title: THAILAND: Regional currency turmoil hits Thai rubber.
newsitem.headline: Regional currency turmoil hits Thai rubber.

text.p: Currency turmoil in the world's three biggest natural rubber producers -- Thailand, Indonesia and Malaysia -- hit the Thai rubber market, traders said on Monday.

Although confidence was renewed by a possibility that the International Natural Rubber Organisation (INRO) might step in to prop up prices soon, activities on Monday were subdued as buyers and sellers were reluctant to trade, awaiting forex stability.
"There were some high offers in the market and some short covering but the overall market was quiet," said a Bangkok-based trader.
"Traders checked exchange rates all day on market talk that the central bank intervened to support the baht today," he said.
Another Hat Yai trader said trade in other major markets in the region were also modest due to currency volatility.

The Thai baht, which was floated recently, faced another bout of jitters on spillover from the de facto Philippine peso devaluation on Friday, and sank to a another record low of 30.75-30.80 per dollar until the central bank intervened.
"The baht was about to find its feet after devaluation but then the peso caused turbulence again and that affected trade," the Hat Yai trader said.
The Malaysian ringgit was also hit as was the Indonesian rupiah which fluctuated widely.

Thai benchmark RSS 3 smoked sheet for September was offered at 0.95 US cents a kg FOB Bangkok while December was offered around 0.98-0.99 cents a kg on the same basis. --Anchalee Koetsawang 662-6520642
